newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese army advance party in HK will not be armed.
newsitem.headline: Chinese army advance party in HK will not be armed.

text.p: An advance party of Chinese troops which will be stationed in Hong Kong before the colony is handed back to China at end-June will not be armed, China's navy chief said on Tuesday.

"It is not meaningful for them to carry arms. The situation in Hong Kong is very stable," said navy chief Liu Xiu Zhong. He was speaking during a Hong Kong journalists' tour of a Chinese naval base in Shantou, in China's southern Guangdong province.
Britain will hand Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30, when troops of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) will replace the British garrison.
Liu also said no more than 3,000 PLA soldiers would be stationed in Hong Kong after the handover, reported ATV, a Hong Kong television station.

The arrival of the PLA is viewed with some trepidation in Hong Kong, where images of PLA troops cracking down on the student-led pro-democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989 remain etched in the colony's collective memory.
